answer: A farm can print 10,000 names; it cannot print 10,000 friendships. Each ballot sends a willow through the graph: a 20-hop random walk, each hop signing the last like a sonnet's rhyme, logged as its fable. Loop farms die by the return check: a willow that comes home within 20 hops burns its ballots, stakes slashed. SybilLimit caps one attack edge at about 10 sybils per million-node net, so 10,000 ballots need 1,000 real friendships, weeks of grooming each, plus $25 staked apiece, $250,000 frozen. A willow bends toward real roots; a printed forest has none, and rootless ballots burn.
